problem: The rewritten is_empty (return lo >= hi) now treats a closed single-point interval (lo == hi with both ends closed, e.g. [5,5]) as empty, whereas it is a valid non-empty singleton set; this silently drops or corrupts results in parse_all, intersect_two/intersection, and complement/difference wherever a closed degenerate point arises.
suggested_fix: Restore the distinction between the two cases, e.g. return lo > hi or (lo == hi and not (lo_closed and hi_closed)).
